summary.oneLiner: Self-funded IDDM defence-product house riding the global shift from "if attacked" to "when attacked." FY26 was a **trough year — rev -29% (₹687.7cr), Q4 rev -45% YoY** — because Operation Sindoor diverted government procurement to emergency anti-drone buys and *delayed* the regular simulator orders; the bulk of the ₹1,336cr order book now executes from FY27. Management reiterates the **₹4,000cr cumulative revenue target across FY27+FY28** and is pivoting from a pure product-builder to a **"facilitator"** orchestrating an ecosystem of subsidiaries/associates (ARI, UTS, AI-Turing, Vector Technics) launching a wave of new products: HyperStrike $10k interceptor drone, Vrishabh UGV, 30mm smart ammunition, CIWS gun-missile, cyber suite.
summary.business: Zen Technologies, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Hyderabad, designs, develops and manufactures its own defence technologies and retains ownership of the underlying intellectual property. Its offerings run across three lines: training solutions including live ranges and virtual simulation, counter-drone detection and neutralisation technologies, and advanced military hardware including robotic surveillance systems and remote weapon stations. Customers are the Ministry of Defence and the Indian armed forces, central and state police, paramilitary and security forces, and allied foreign armed forces, with a presence across India, the UAE and the United States.

Training solutions and live ranges: Smart Target System (Zen STS) with LOMAH
Weapon stations and combat robotics: Barbarik AI-powered Remote Controlled Weapon Station
Parashu AI-powered Remote Controlled Weapon Station
Compact gun-and-missile system for naval forces

currentContext.expansion: The Company is expanding its research footprint to meet demand for autonomous and aerial defence solutions. A new R&D and manufacturing facility is being developed at the Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) in Tuem, Goa — described as an upcoming 'Advanced R&D' facility — while the Company continues to build its software and AI development capability for combat robotics and autonomous systems. Its existing footprint comprises the R&D Centre at Sanath Nagar, Hyderabad (recognised by the Ministry of Science and Technology, and dedicated to next-generation simulation platforms and anti-drone architectures), a Demo Centre cum Factory near Shamshabad Airport that showcases training ecosystems and counter-drone systems to domestic and international clients, and the Software and AI Development Centre at Kondapur, Hyderabad, which supports deep-learning models for the Hawkeye platforms and adaptive-learning models for simulators in secure, air-gapped environments. The Maheshwaram unit in Hyderabad was commissioned in 2009. Capital commitments outstanding at the balance-sheet date relate to construction of a new factory building and others. On the product side, the Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle — 150 kg payload, up to 50 km/h, range up to 100 km, indigenous content above 85% — is planned for commercial launch in FY27, and the Hyperstrike loitering strike platform is designed for scaled production, with its high-speed propulsion system supplied by subsidiary Vector Technics.

risks.risk: Order finalisation and conversion timing — lumpy, milestone-based defence contracts
risks.note: Management attributes the FY26 revenue moderation to delays in order finalisation, shifting procurement priorities and the milestone-based nature of defence contracts; order conversion timing extended beyond expectations, pushing the bulk of recent orders into FY27. The AR separately flags 'order-book uncertainty': developing bespoke systems without finalised orders can pressure cash flows, mitigated by prioritising milestone-based agreements.

risks.risk: Customer and activity concentration on a single government buyer base
risks.note: BRSR reports 100% of turnover from one activity — designing, developing and manufacturing combat training solutions for homeland security and counter-drone technology — sold principally to the Ministry of Defence, allied foreign armed forces, state police, security and paramilitary organisations. Exports contributed only 0.14% of total turnover, so the revenue line is effectively tied to Indian government procurement cycles and budget priorities.

risks.risk: Procurement structure biased to the lowest bidder
risks.note: Tender processes often favour the lowest bidder, which may not reflect lifecycle value; the Company responds with cost optimisation and lean manufacturing while delivering the technological value required for mission success.

risks.risk: Competitive dynamics — aggressive pricing by global players
risks.note: Global players may use aggressive pricing to secure large contracts; the Company relies on deep product customisation, superior technical performance and long-term service relationships to defend value beyond the initial purchase price.

risks.risk: Technological obsolescence in a fast-moving capability race
risks.note: Rapid innovation carries the risk of systems becoming outdated; mitigation is continuous investment in next-generation research, agile development and strategic partnerships. The BRSR frames technological advancement as a material issue whose flip side is loss of competitive advantage.

risks.risk: Cyber security, data privacy and IP theft
risks.note: As a defence-sector organisation entrusted with sensitive information, a threat-sensitive environment makes the Company a target for digital incursion and intellectual-property theft; breaches could bring legal repercussions, reputational damage and substantial financial losses. Mitigation is a Cyber Risk Management framework, regular security assessments, strict data-access control and encryption, alongside ISO/IEC 27001 adherence.

Geopolitical instability and component shortages can delay production, causing higher costs and customer dissatisfaction; mitigation is a resilient, multi-tiered and diverse supplier network, regular risk assessments, contingency planning and real-time monitoring.

Specialised defence-technology talent is in high global demand and high turnover raises recruitment cost and destroys accumulated expertise; the permanent-employee turnover rate was 14.01% in FY 2025-26 (16.96% in FY 2024-25). Mitigation is a mission-driven culture, attractive compensation, clear growth pathways and succession planning.

guidance / outlook:
- **₹4,000cr cumulative revenue across FY27+FY28** (reaffirmed); ~₹2,500–3,000cr in FY28 implied. Order book expected to *touch* ₹3,000cr at some point.
- **~₹1,000cr of the ₹1,336cr order book executes in FY27** (mostly Q2–Q3 FY27); balance ₹326cr is AMC spread over contract life.
- Long-term margin guidance **35% operational EBITDA / 25% PAT — "remain intact."**
- New-order inflow expected to *accelerate* in FY27; "good news" expected **in Q1, not later than Q2 FY27.**
- Subsidiaries: **UTS + ARI together ~₹365cr revenue in FY27**; longer-term ARI ~₹300cr, UTS ₹150–200cr (margins ~27–31%).
- WC cycle to normalize to **140–150 days** longer-term (elevated now on inventory build for FY27 deliveries).
order book & pipeline:
- Consol order book **₹1,336cr** (standalone ₹1,222.6cr) as on 31-Mar-26; ARI ₹75cr, UTS ₹35cr closing (vs opening ARI ₹90cr, UTS ₹110cr).
- Bidding pipeline: **~₹1,500cr competitive tenders + "couple of thousand crores" single-vendor/nomination** → total pipeline "running into a few thousand crores" (regular tenders may take ~18 months).
- Pipeline split tilts **~55:45 in favour of anti-drone vs simulators**.
- **Hard-kill anti-drone orders started arriving: ~₹40cr** received (L70 integration); repeat + upgrade orders flowing from Operation Sindoor lessons.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Standalone ₹423cr; subsidiaries ₹260cr** of FY26 consol ₹688cr. ARI contributed ₹131cr (PAT margin ~30.3%); UTS the bulk of the rest (PAT margin ~26.5%); other subs ~₹10cr.
- ARI (under Commodore Ahluwalia) + ANAWAVE freed bandwidth via AI productivity → developed cyber suite, anti-drone simulator, etc. ARI has South America / Europe connections for naval-sim export push.
- AI-Turing (associate): co-developed 30mm RF-programmable pre-frag ammunition and CIWS gun-missile system.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **HyperStrike interceptor/loiter drone** — $10k cost vs $30k Shahed, 400 km/h, 5-min loiter, 20km+ range, AI tracking + manual override, capacity 5,000/shift/month scalable to 15,000; production starts FY27. Mgmt: *"could be the largest product in our portfolio two years out."*
- **Counter-drone hardware:** widened frequency dominance **70 MHz–12 GHz** (vs 400 MHz–6 GHz earlier), 15km+ detection, indigenized 20km radar, RF/GNSS jamming + RCWS/L70/ZU-23 hard-kill.
- **Vrishabh UGV** (combat/logistics/casualty-evac, 150kg payload, 50 km/h, 100km range, >85% indigenous) — commercial launch FY27.
- **30mm smart ammunition** (10×10m kill radius, anti-drone, no weapon modification) — manufacture/supply from FY27.
- **Cybersecurity suite ("Suraksha")** — 6-layer, post-quantum-ready, zero foreign dependency; for command centres/ships/aircraft.
- **Naval simulation** (mine-clearance, choke-point e.g. Hormuz) — full combat naval training centres; export interest via ARI.
- **Arms & ammunition licences** (granted) — meaningful from FY28/year-3.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 op-EBITDA margin 28.6% is below the 35% target purely on the 5 transient/one-off items above; FY26 still 35.95%.
- Hardware mix concern addressed: hardware was *always* a major part of products (simulators/anti-drone); only non-critical manufacturing is outsourced — assembly/QA/dispatch in-house. Mgmt sees **no threat to 35% EBITDA / 25% PAT** for next couple of years; "addicted to margins" → only smart (not dumb) ammunition.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Asset-light "facilitator" model retained even for arms/ammo: outsource most production, manufacture only critical components in-house.
- Capacity already cited for HyperStrike (5,000→15,000/month). No large capex figure disclosed; debt-free with ₹1,308cr cash funds the build.
capital allocation:
- **Debt-free; ₹1,308cr cash.** Self-funds R&D (key differentiator vs DRDO-co-funded peers).
- **M&A active:** scouting acquisitions in simulators, anti-drone, and "Pareto technologies" (20% of tech that decides 80% of war); model = supply capital + ecosystem guidance to focused small companies.
risks & watch-items:
- **Order-timing risk:** FY27 is heavily back-end-loaded (Q2–Q3 execution); any slip on the awaited Q1/Q2 inflows dents the ₹4,000cr cumulative target.
- **Policy risk:** draft DAP language equating ToT/foreign-IP "made in India" with IDDM could blunt the self-funded innovator's edge — mgmt lobbying against it.
- **Foreign-procurement pull:** armed-forces preference for ready foreign "patch-up" buys in the near term (mgmt downplays it strongly).
- **Frequency "catch-up game":** adversary drones shifting bands (10 MHz–12 GHz) force constant counter-drone R&D — structurally elevated R&D cost base.
- Ammunition certification complexity ("two-year period should be sufficient").
- Lumpy, government-dependent ordering; elevated working capital during execution years.
management quality / tone: - Highly confident, mission-driven, candid on the trough quarter and one-offs. Ashok Atluri visionary/colourful (Godfather, Pareto-recursion, "make Shahed into Shaheed"); CFO precise and numbers-grounded. Strong skin-in-the-game (self-funded R&D, debt-free). Tone: FY26 a deliberate dip, FY27 the inflection; 2026 framed as a "hallmark year" for indigenous IDDM innovators.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The revenue collapse is a feature, not a bug:** Operation Sindoor *pulled forward* emergency anti-drone orders while *pushing out* regular simulator orders — so the ₹1,336cr book + accelerating pipeline matters far more than the -45% Q4.
- **Business-model pivot to "facilitator":** Zen increasingly orchestrates an ecosystem (ARI/UTS/AI-Turing/Vector Technics) rather than building everything itself — AI-driven productivity freed the bandwidth for the product wave.
- **Interceptor-drone economics** ($10k kill of $30k Shahed) directly attack the "$3m missile vs $30k drone" cost-inversion problem — potentially the single biggest future product and a global export story.
- Hard-kill + ammunition + arms licences shift Zen up the kill-chain from detect/jam into the actual neutralization hardware (RCWS, 30mm smart ammo, CIWS) — higher-value, stickier.
- DSO improved 42 days even in a weak revenue quarter — collections quality intact.

FY26 was a **trough year — rev -29% (₹687.7cr), Q4 rev -45% YoY** — because Operation Sindoor diverted government procurement to emergency anti-drone buys and *delayed* the regular simulator orders; the bulk of the ₹1,336cr order book now executes from FY27. risks & watch-items:
- **Order-timing risk:** FY27 is heavily back-end-loaded (Q2–Q3 execution); any slip on the awaited Q1/Q2 inflows dents the ₹4,000cr cumulative target.
- **Policy risk:** draft DAP language equating ToT/foreign-IP "made in India" with IDDM could blunt the self-funded innovator's edge — mgmt lobbying against it.
- **Foreign-procurement pull:** armed-forces preference for ready foreign "patch-up" buys in the near term (mgmt downplays it strongly).
- **Frequency "catch-up game":** adversary drones shifting bands (10 MHz–12 GHz) force constant counter-drone R&D — structurally elevated R&D cost base.
- Ammunition certification complexity ("two-year period should be sufficient").
- Lumpy, government-dependent ordering; elevated working capital during execution years.
management quality / tone: - Highly confident, mission-driven, candid on the trough quarter and one-offs. Ashok Atluri visionary/colourful (Godfather, Pareto-recursion, "make Shahed into Shaheed"); CFO precise and numbers-grounded. Strong skin-in-the-game (self-funded R&D, debt-free). Tone: FY26 a deliberate dip, FY27 the inflection; 2026 framed as a "hallmark year" for indigenous IDDM innovators.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The revenue collapse is a feature, not a bug:** Operation Sindoor *pulled forward* emergency anti-drone orders while *pushing out* regular simulator orders — so the ₹1,336cr book + accelerating pipeline matters far more than the -45% Q4.
- **Business-model pivot to "facilitator":** Zen increasingly orchestrates an ecosystem (ARI/UTS/AI-Turing/Vector Technics) rather than building everything itself — AI-driven productivity freed the bandwidth for the product wave.
- **Interceptor-drone economics** ($10k kill of $30k Shahed) directly attack the "$3m missile vs $30k drone" cost-inversion problem — potentially the single biggest future product and a global export story.
- Hard-kill + ammunition + arms licences shift Zen up the kill-chain from detect/jam into the actual neutralization hardware (RCWS, 30mm smart ammo, CIWS) — higher-value, stickier.
- DSO improved 42 days even in a weak revenue quarter — collections quality intact.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Zen Technologies, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Hyderabad, designs, develops and manufactures its own defence technologies and retains ownership of the underlying intellectual property. Its offerings run across three lines: training solutions including live ranges and virtual simulation, counter-drone detection and neutralisation technologies, and advanced military hardware including robotic surveillance systems and remote weapon stations. Customers are the Ministry of Defence and the Indian armed forces, central and state police, paramilitary and security forces, and allied foreign armed forces, with a presence across India, the UAE and the United States.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- FY26 revenue moderation was attributed to delays in order finalisation, shifting procurement priorities and the milestone-based nature of defence contracts; order conversion timing extended beyond management's expectations, with the bulk of recent orders scheduled for execution from FY27.
- Management states underlying momentum remained robust across simulation systems, counter-UAS technologies and emerging autonomous platforms.
- Management expects the draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 to compress the procurement cycle considerably and to open new growth opportunities for companies with genuine indigenous capability and intellectual property; it also expects order wins to begin flowing through in the near term.
- DAP 2026 introduces Long-Term Bulk Acquisition, giving industry ten-year visibility on orders, and Low-Cost Capital Acquisition for fast-moving technologies such as drones and artificial intelligence, with emphasis on indigenously designed, developed and manufactured technologies.
- The Union Budget for FY27 carried a record allocation of approximately ₹7.85 lakh crore to the Ministry of Defence, up about 15.19%, with approximately ₹1.85 lakh crore towards capital acquisitions of advanced platforms, weapon systems, drones and counter-drone technologies, and about 75% of the capital acquisition budget earmarked for domestic defence firms.
- India's counter-drone market is projected to grow at a 24.4% compound annual rate to reach US$1.39 billion by 2030.
- Demand for layered anti-drone systems has surged in the wake of regional conflicts, with a shift towards wide-band electronic warfare solutions able to disrupt communication and navigation across non-standard frequencies — the design premise of the Company's own system.
- The military is moving towards Integrated Combat Training Nodes that combine live firing with virtual and constructive simulation, and the Indian Army has declared 2026 the year of Networking and Data Centricity.
- The private sector's contribution to defence production has climbed to 23%, with order books for private firms estimated to reach ₹55,000 crore by the end of FY26.
- Indigenous defence production reached approximately ₹1.54 lakh crore in FY25 with FY26 projected to surpass the ₹1.75 lakh crore target; defence exports reportedly reached an all-time high of approximately ₹38,424 crore in FY26.
- Subsidiaries and associates — Applied Research International, Vector Technics, Bhairav Robotics and AI Turing — added to consolidated revenue and earnings, described by management as validating past capital allocation decisions.
- Results should be read within the context of the defence sector's procurement cycles; the strong FY25 revenue base was driven by concentrated order execution.
- Consolidated order book of ₹1,336.04 crore at the close of FY26 (approximately ₹1,336 crore as at 31 March 2026), described as providing strong revenue visibility.
- Standalone order book stood at ₹1,222.6 crore.
- New order inflows of ₹431.36 crore were secured during the fourth quarter alone.
- The majority of the order book is scheduled for execution from FY27, and about ₹1,000 crore is expected to convert into revenue during that year.
- Order-book uncertainty is a flagged risk: developing bespoke systems without finalised orders can pressure cash flows, mitigated by prioritising milestone-based agreements.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is expanding its research footprint to meet demand for autonomous and aerial defence solutions. A new R&D and manufacturing facility is being developed at the Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) in Tuem, Goa — described as an upcoming 'Advanced R&D' facility — while the Company continues to build its software and AI development capability for combat robotics and autonomous systems. Its existing footprint comprises the R&D Centre at Sanath Nagar, Hyderabad (recognised by the Ministry of Science and Technology, and dedicated to next-generation simulation platforms and anti-drone architectures), a Demo Centre cum Factory near Shamshabad Airport that showcases training ecosystems and counter-drone systems to domestic and international clients, and the Software and AI Development Centre at Kondapur, Hyderabad, which supports deep-learning models for the Hawkeye platforms and adaptive-learning models for simulators in secure, air-gapped environments. The Maheshwaram unit in Hyderabad was commissioned in 2009. Capital commitments outstanding at the balance-sheet date relate to construction of a new factory building and others. On the product side, the Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle — 150 kg payload, up to 50 km/h, range up to 100 km, indigenous content above 85% — is planned for commercial launch in FY27, and the Hyperstrike loitering strike platform is designed for scaled production, with its high-speed propulsion system supplied by subsidiary Vector Technics.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Owns the intellectual property behind its technologies, built through sustained self-funded research rather than licensed assembly, which aligns it with a procurement framework that rewards indigenously designed, developed and manufactured systems
- 94 patents granted to date and the CII Best Patent Portfolio Award 2025, with ₹139.11 crore invested in R&D over the last five years
- Combat validation: its Counter-UAS system was deployed during Operation Sindoor, detecting up to 100 drone threats at a time with a response time under 0.1 seconds and neutralising hundreds of drones and swarm drones
- Wide-band engineering choice — the Counter-UAS system detects and jams drone data links well beyond the commercial 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands, where conventional solutions struggle
- Breadth across five capabilities — training simulation, counter-drone, automated weapon stations, combat robotics and drones — assembled through acquisitions, associates and partnerships
- Over three decades of operating history with 1,000+ training systems shipped worldwide
- Debt-free balance sheet with cash and bank balances of over ₹1,308 crore and the highest Dun & Bradstreet rating of 5A1, reflecting capacity to handle large government contracts
- Government licence under the Arms Act for manufacture of specified weapon systems, together with an ammunition licence

risks.body:
- **Order-timing risk:** FY27 is heavily back-end-loaded (Q2–Q3 execution); any slip on the awaited Q1/Q2 inflows dents the ₹4,000cr cumulative target.
- **Policy risk:** draft DAP language equating ToT/foreign-IP "made in India" with IDDM could blunt the self-funded innovator's edge — mgmt lobbying against it.
- **Foreign-procurement pull:** armed-forces preference for ready foreign "patch-up" buys in the near term (mgmt downplays it strongly).
- **Frequency "catch-up game":** adversary drones shifting bands (10 MHz–12 GHz) force constant counter-drone R&D — structurally elevated R&D cost base.
- Ammunition certification complexity ("two-year period should be sufficient").
- Lumpy, government-dependent ordering; elevated working capital during execution years.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The revenue collapse is a feature, not a bug:** Operation Sindoor *pulled forward* emergency anti-drone orders while *pushing out* regular simulator orders — so the ₹1,336cr book + accelerating pipeline matters far more than the -45% Q4.
- **Business-model pivot to "facilitator":** Zen increasingly orchestrates an ecosystem (ARI/UTS/AI-Turing/Vector Technics) rather than building everything itself — AI-driven productivity freed the bandwidth for the product wave.
- **Interceptor-drone economics** ($10k kill of $30k Shahed) directly attack the "$3m missile vs $30k drone" cost-inversion problem — potentially the single biggest future product and a global export story.
- Hard-kill + ammunition + arms licences shift Zen up the kill-chain from detect/jam into the actual neutralization hardware (RCWS, 30mm smart ammo, CIWS) — higher-value, stickier.
- DSO improved 42 days even in a weak revenue quarter — collections quality intact.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** trough year (rev -29% FY, -45% Q4 YoY) on Sindoor-driven order delay; Q4 op-EBITDA 28.6% on 5 one-offs (FY 35.95%); order book ₹1,336cr (~₹1,000cr executes FY27, Q2–Q3); ₹4,000cr FY27+FY28 target reaffirmed; debt-free, ₹1,308cr cash; new products launched (HyperStrike $10k interceptor, Vrishabh UGV, 30mm smart ammo, CIWS, cyber suite); pipeline ~₹1,500cr competitive + several '000cr nomination, ~55:45 anti-drone:sim; hard-kill orders began (~₹40cr); arms/ammo licences granted (material FY28+); ARI ₹131cr / UTS bulk; FY27 subs ~₹365cr.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: the promised Q1/Q2 order inflows (key de-risk), ₹1,000cr book conversion pace, margin recovery toward 35% as revenue ramps, HyperStrike/UGV/ammo production starts, M&A announcements, WC normalization toward 140–150 days._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Policy] Domestically, "the draft Defence Acquisition Procedure 2026 and the broader policy push towards Buy Indian IDDM continue to intensify the tailwinds initiated by late Mr Manohar Parikkar".
- [Order book bridge] Order book moved from Rs 1082.76 Cr at 1st January 2026, plus new orders of Rs 431.36 Cr bagged in Q4FY26, less Rs 178.08 Cr executed in Q4FY26, to Rs 1336.04 Crore at 31st March 2026.
- [Guidance framing] Management explicitly flags "FY26 financial performance was muted relative to FY25, a trajectory we have communicated earlier to our investors and stakeholders", while asserting "FY27 execution is clearly visible".
